title: BlockSmoothConvexConcave.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: The objective is convex in x for every fixed y and concave in y for every fixed x; strong convexity and strong concavity are not required.

problem_class.label: saddle_point
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization–maximization on E × F, with an existing global saddle point (xs,ys).

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Each query requests either gx(x,y)=∇x f(x,y) or gy(x,y)=∇y f(x,y). Replies are exact and independent of call index and oracle seed. Evaluating both partial gradients costs two oracle calls.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/BlockSmoothConvexConcave.lean: spec.Query, spec.Reply and spec.admissible, oracle.answer equalities and HasGradientAt conditions; LongTails/Template.lean: execute.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: E and F are arbitrary complete real inner-product spaces. Globally, gx is Lx-Lipschitz in x and Lxy-Lipschitz in y; gy is Ly-Lipschitz in y and Lxy-Lipschitz in x. All three constants are nonnegative, with Lx+Lxy>0 and Ly+Lxy>0. A saddle point satisfies ‖x0−xs‖²+‖y0−ys‖²≤R². Spaces, smoothness constants, x0,y0,γ,δ are public; R≥0 and ε>0 are hidden from algorithm construction. Valid parameters require 1<γ≤2 and δ≥1. The allowed family is specified through alexGda with positive α,β.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/BlockSmoothConvexConcave.lean: Public, Params, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, spec.admissible and spec.allowedAlgorithm; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence.makeAlgorithm.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm_squared
accuracy.details: The returned pair (x,y) must satisfy ‖∇x f(x,y)‖²+‖∇y f(x,y)‖²≤ε². No objective-gap, distance, averaging, or last-iterate requirement is imposed by successful.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The squared joint-gradient bound holds almost surely under the joint algorithm-seed and oracle-seed law. The oracle-call budget holds for every seed.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/BlockSmoothConvexConcave.lean: spec.successful, ∀ᵐ condition; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence, product probability law and ∀ seed cost bound.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: Smooth unconstrained convex–concave saddle optimization with exact first-order information and a gradient-residual accuracy criterion is an established formulation, including Hilbert-space versions and separate block smoothness bounds.

descriptionHtml:
Alex-GDA for Block-Smooth Saddle Problems

We consider minx∈Emaxy∈Ff(x,y) on real Hilbert spaces E and F, where f:E×F→R is convex in x, concave in y, and has globally Lipschitz partial gradients in each variable. A given starting pair (x0,y0) lies within distance R≥0 of a saddle point in the Hilbert product norm. Each oracle query returns either ∇xf(x,y) or ∇yf(x,y). For ε>0, Alex-GDA must return (x¯,y¯) satisfying ∥∇xf(x¯,y¯)∥2+∥∇yf(x¯,y¯)∥2≤ε2 almost surely.

The saddle-point problem is minx∈Emaxy∈Ff(x,y). Norms on E and F are induced by their inner products, and we use the product norm ∥(x,y)∥=(∥x∥2+∥y∥2)1/2. The block constants satisfy Lx,Ly,Lxy≥0,Lx+Lxy>0,Ly+Lxy>0. The algorithm receives E,F,Lx,Ly,Lxy, the starting pair (x0,y0), and parameters γ,δ satisfying 1<γ≤2 and δ≥1; the radius R and tolerance ε may enter only the oracle-call budget.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Convexity and concavity). For every y∈F, the function f(⋅,y) is convex on E. For every x∈E, the function f(x,⋅) is concave on F.

Assumption 2 (Block smoothness). Both partial functions are Fréchet differentiable everywhere. For all x,x′∈E and y,y′∈F, their gradients satisfy ∥∇xf(x,y)−∇xf(x′,y)∥≤Lx∥x−x′∥,∥∇xf(x,y)−∇xf(x,y′)∥≤Lxy∥y−y′∥,∥∇yf(x,y)−∇yf(x,y′)∥≤Ly∥y−y′∥,∥∇yf(x,y)−∇yf(x′,y)∥≤Lxy∥x−x′∥.

Assumption 3 (Saddle point and initial distance). There exists (x⋆,y⋆)∈E×F such that, for every x∈E and y∈F, f(x⋆,y)≤f(x⋆,y⋆)≤f(x,y⋆), and ∥x0−x⋆∥2+∥y0−y⋆∥2≤R2.

Queries may be made at any pair in E×F. The oracle returns the requested exact partial gradient, with each partial-gradient evaluation counted as one call.

Our result is algorithm-specific: we analyze Alex-GDA. The method chooses fixed step sizes α,β>0 from its available inputs and initializes v0=0. Starting from the given pair, each iteration k≥0 makes two successive oracle calls and updates according to gk=∇xf(xk,yk+(δ−1)βvk),hk=∇yf(xk−γαgk,yk),xk+1=xk−αgk,yk+1=yk+βhk,vk+1=hk. For each completed iteration, define sk=∥gk∥2+∥hk∥2+∥vk∥2. Given a total budget of B≥0 oracle calls, let N=⌊B/2⌋. If N≥1, the output is the pre-update pair with the smallest score, with ties resolved by the earliest index: k⋆=minargmin0≤k<N⁡sk,(x¯,y¯)=(xk⋆,yk⋆). If N=0, the output is (x0,y0). An unpaired final partial-gradient call does not change the output.

The required accuracy is the squared gradient-residual bound ∥∇xf(x¯,y¯)∥2+∥∇yf(x¯,y¯)∥2≤ε2P-a.s., where P is the law of the algorithm’s randomness; the specified method and exact replies are deterministic.

theorems.referencesHtml:
• G. M. Korpelevich. The Extragradient Method for Finding Saddle Points and Other Problems. 1976; English translation 1977. Complexity: O(1+(max{Lx,Ly}+Lxy)2R2/ε2) fixed exact partial-gradient calls for joint gradient norm at most ε, using extragradient with best-iterate selection; four partial-gradient calls per iteration, no additional initialization calls, and zero calls when R=0.
  • Taeho Yoon and Ernest K. Ryu. Accelerated Algorithms for Smooth Convex-Concave Minimax Problems with O(1/k²) Rate on Squared Gradient Norm. 2021. Complexity: O(1+(max{Lx,Ly}+Lxy)R/ε) fixed exact partial-gradient calls for last-iterate joint gradient norm at most ε, using extra anchored gradient; four partial-gradient calls per iteration and no additional initialization calls.
theorems.formulaHtml: 2⋅⌈180⋅γ4⋅δ4⋅(max{Lx,Ly}+Lxy)2⋅R2(γ−1)3⋅ε2⌉+

comparisonHtml:
On real Hilbert spaces E×F, f is differentiable and convex–concave. Its partial gradients have within-block Lipschitz bounds Lx,Ly≥0 and cross-block bound Lxy≥0, with Lx+Lxy,Ly+Lxy>0. A saddle z⋆ satisfies ∥z0−z⋆∥≤R, where R≥0. Exact partial-gradient queries are available. The setup requires constant-step Alex-GDA with 1<γ≤2, δ≥1. The target is ∥∇xf(z^)∥2+∥∇yf(z^)∥2≤ε2, ε>0; (1) achieves it deterministically at a selected iterate. Other algorithm families below compare the underlying problem and oracle on the stated restrictions.

Comparison for BlockSmoothConvexConcave.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) AlexGdaConvexConcave (Ours) (review) O(1+γ4δ4Λ2R2(γ−1)3ε2)
(2) EAG-V (Yoon and Ryu 2021, Cor. 2) O(1+ΛR/ε); four block calls per iteration. Finite-dimensional statement; last-iterate accuracy. (1): No established improvement on the finite-dimensional overlap. (1): For fixed γ,δ and ΛR/ε>1, quadratic rather than linear cost; selected rather than last iterate; needs separate block bounds instead of Λ.
(3) Optimistic gradient / PEG (Gorbunov et al. 2022, Thm. 1) O(1+Λ2R2/ε2); two block calls per iteration, including initialization. Finite-dimensional unconstrained specialization; last-iterate accuracy. (1): Matches known rate for fixed γ,δ on the finite-dimensional overlap, with the same oracle access. (1): Selected rather than last iterate; at least tenfold larger leading constant; deteriorates as γ↓1 or δ grows.
(4) Alternating GDA, momentum −12 (Shugart et al. 2026, Thm. 3.1) O(1+Λ2R2/ε2); two block calls per iteration. Finite dimensions; E∥∇f(zτ)∥2≤ε2 for uniform τ. (1): Deterministic selected output instead of expected random-iterate accuracy; matches the rate for fixed γ,δ on the finite-dimensional overlap.
(5) Derived bound (Shugart et al. 2026, Thm. 3.1) O(1+Λ2R2/ε2); three block calls per iteration including residual selection. Finite dimensions; deterministic minimum-residual iterate. (1): No extra selection queries; two rather than three calls per iteration. Matched total-cost order for fixed γ,δ, not a proved total-cost saving.
(6) Alex-GDA (Lee et al. 2024, Thm. 5.1; Conj. 8.2) No general convex–concave bound in Thm. 5.1: requires twice-differentiable, finite-dimensional, strongly convex–strongly concave objectives and γ,δ>1. (1): Method-specific scope extension to mere convexity–concavity, including δ=1; selected-iterate stationarity partially addresses Conj. 8.2, without establishing its last-iterate convergence claim.

Abbr: Λ=max{Lx,Ly}+Lxy; z0=(x0,y0); ∥∇f(z)∥2=∥∇xf(z)∥2+∥∇yf(z)∥2. Costs count individual partial-gradient calls. EAG: extra anchored gradient; PEG: past extragradient; GDA: gradient descent–ascent.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.ProbabilityMeasure

namespace OracleTemplate.BlockSaddle

universe u v

structure AlexState (E : Type u) (F : Type v) where
  phase : Bool
  n : ℕ
  x : E
  y : F
  v : F
  g : E
  best : E × F
  bestVal : ℝ

variable {E : Type u} {F : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [InnerProductSpace ℝ F]

noncomputable def alexGda (γ δ α β : ℝ) (x0 : E) (y0 : F) :
    Algorithm ((E × F) ⊕ (E × F)) (E ⊕ F) (E × F) where
  State := AlexState E F
  initial := fun _ => ⟨false, 0, x0, y0, 0, 0, (x0, y0), 0⟩
  query :=  fun st => (0,
    if st.phase then Sum.inr (st.x - (γ * α) • st.g, st.y)
    else Sum.inl (st.x, st.y + ((δ - 1) * β) • st.v))
  update := fun st r =>
    if st.phase then
      ⟨false, st.n + 1, st.x - α • st.g, st.y + β • Sum.elim (fun _ => (0 : F)) id r,
        Sum.elim (fun _ => (0 : F)) id r, 0,
        if st.n = 0 ∨
            ‖st.g‖ ^ 2 + ‖Sum.elim (fun _ => (0 : F)) id r‖ ^ 2 + ‖st.v‖ ^ 2 < st.bestVal then
          (st.x, st.y) else st.best,
        if st.n = 0 ∨
            ‖st.g‖ ^ 2 + ‖Sum.elim (fun _ => (0 : F)) id r‖ ^ 2 + ‖st.v‖ ^ 2 < st.bestVal then
          ‖st.g‖ ^ 2 + ‖Sum.elim (fun _ => (0 : F)) id r‖ ^ 2 + ‖st.v‖ ^ 2 else st.bestVal⟩
    else ⟨true, st.n, st.x, st.y, st.v, Sum.elim id (fun _ => (0 : E)) r, st.best, st.bestVal⟩
  output := fun st => st.best

end OracleTemplate.BlockSaddle

open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.BlockSmoothConvexConcave

open OracleTemplate OracleTemplate.BlockSaddle

structure Public where
  E : Type u
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  F : Type u
  [normedF : NormedAddCommGroup F]
  [linearF : InnerProductSpace ℝ F]
  [completeF : CompleteSpace F]
  Lx : ℝ
  Ly : ℝ
  Lxy : ℝ
  γ : ℝ
  δ : ℝ
  x0 : E
  y0 : F

attribute [instance] Public.normedE Public.linearE Public.completeE Public.normedF
  Public.linearF Public.completeF

structure Params extends Public where
  R : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance p := p.E → p.F → ℝ
  Query p := (p.E × p.F) ⊕ (p.E × p.F)
  Reply p := p.E ⊕ p.F
  Output p := p.E × p.F
  publicInput := Params.toPublic
  valid q :=
    0 ≤ q.Lx ∧ 0 ≤ q.Ly ∧ 0 ≤ q.Lxy ∧ 0 < q.Lx + q.Lxy ∧ 0 < q.Ly + q.Lxy ∧
    1 < q.γ ∧ q.γ ≤ 2 ∧ 1 ≤ q.δ ∧ 0 ≤ q.R ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q f oracle :=
    ∃ (gx : q.E × q.F → q.E) (gy : q.E × q.F → q.F),
      (∀ k seed z, oracle.answer k (0, (Sum.inl z)) seed = Sum.inl (gx z)) ∧
      (∀ k seed z, oracle.answer k (0, (Sum.inr z)) seed = Sum.inr (gy z)) ∧
      (∀ z : q.E × q.F, HasGradientAt (fun x => f x z.2) (gx z) z.1) ∧
      (∀ z : q.E × q.F, HasGradientAt (fun y => f z.1 y) (gy z) z.2) ∧
      (∀ y, ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ (fun x => f x y)) ∧
      (∀ x, ConcaveOn ℝ Set.univ (fun y => f x y)) ∧
      (∀ x x' y, ‖gx (x, y) - gx (x', y)‖ ≤ q.Lx * ‖x - x'‖) ∧
      (∀ x y y', ‖gx (x, y) - gx (x, y')‖ ≤ q.Lxy * ‖y - y'‖) ∧
      (∀ x y y', ‖gy (x, y) - gy (x, y')‖ ≤ q.Ly * ‖y - y'‖) ∧
      (∀ x x' y, ‖gy (x, y) - gy (x', y)‖ ≤ q.Lxy * ‖x - x'‖) ∧
      (∃ xs ys, (∀ x y, f xs y ≤ f xs ys ∧ f xs ys ≤ f x ys) ∧
        ‖q.x0 - xs‖ ^ 2 + ‖q.y0 - ys‖ ^ 2 ≤ q.R ^ 2)
  successful q f output P :=
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : MeasureTheory.Measure _), ∀ (vx : q.E) (vy : q.F),
      HasGradientAt (fun x => f x (output ω).2) vx (output ω).1 →
      HasGradientAt (fun y => f (output ω).1 y) vy (output ω).2 →
      ‖vx‖ ^ 2 + ‖vy‖ ^ 2 ≤ q.ε ^ 2
  allowedAlgorithm p A := ∃ α β : ℝ, 0 < α ∧ 0 < β ∧ A = alexGda p.γ p.δ α β p.x0 p.y0

end LongTails.Setups.BlockSmoothConvexConcave
